features.statement: A single serif font family (Georgia) is used for headings, body, navigation, form labels and footer.
Section headings are set at body-size or modestly larger, with the heading hierarchy not matching visual prominence.
Header uses a dark slate gradient lightening downward, blending into a flat teal page background.
A muted gold/khaki accent colors the active nav tab, primary button and heading rules.
Body text uses a dark blue-grey rather than pure black.
Surfaces are off-white or slightly translucent white rather than pure white.
Links like 'more →' use a distinct bold, underlined red hue found nowhere else.
Footer is a near-black band with small, centered, light-grey copyright text.
Layout has a narrow left sidebar of stacked white cards beside a wider white main content card.
Horizontal nav strip is near-white with a gold bottom rule, bold labels, and a gold-filled active tab.
Logo sits on a white rounded tile with a shadow, scaled down from its natural size.
Sidebar section titles are image banners with torn-paper edges and different lettering, not live text.
Small uppercase letter-spaced labels act as subheadings within lists.
Form labels sit above full-width inputs with thin grey borders and slight rounding.
Contact details use an address element with line breaks and a bold name, listing legacy channels.
Intro section pairs a rotated, scattered-print photo collage with text beside it.
Section headings sit above a thin gold horizontal rule spanning the content width.
Gallery is a multi-column grid of slightly downscaled thumbnails, each in a bordered, padded white frame.
Image alt text is generic and numbered, with no images missing alt.
Corners are small-radius only; no large radii or pill shapes.
No animations or transforms; only simple CSS transitions, likely on link hover.
Page uses semantic landmarks (header, nav, main, aside, footer, sections) with few classes and inline styles.
Page is link-dense with sparse text, with many anchors relative to word count.
Copy is a short, informal first-person-plural welcome opening with a local-language greeting and non-native phrasing.
Heading order in DOM places a sidebar heading before the main heading, with one H1.
Layout relies mostly on CSS grid rather than flexbox.
